newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu to form semiconductor venture in China.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu to form semiconductor venture in China.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Thursday it would form a joint venture in China in June to assemble and test semiconductor products.

Fujitsu agreed with Nantong Huada Microelectronics Co Ltd to form the venture, to be capitalised at $10 million, which will assemble and test integrated circuit (IC) products in Nantong, Jiangsu Province, the Japanese computer company said in a statement.
The new firm, Nantong Fujitsu Microelectronics Co Ltd, will be 40 percent owned by a Fujitsu unit in China and 60 percent owned by the Chinese partner, Fujitsu said.
The new company will assemble and test logic ICs, including micro controllers and linear ICs for consumer products, it said.

Nantong Huada's existing factory will be used initially, with monthly production capacity of 10 million units, Fujitsu said. A new factory, with monthly production capacity of 40 million units, will be built by the end of March 1999, it said.
The venture plans to expand its production line-up in the future by adding the assembly of memory products, Fujitsu said.
